summary: This government bill would create the 'Maldives Digital Identity System', a legal way to prove who you are online and offline with government offices, companies and other people. Maldives Digital Services would run it, register people, issue each person a digital ID number, tokens and authenticators, approve digital wallets, and set the technical and security rules. Maldivian ID card holders, foreign workers with work permits and their dependants on visas could sign up, giving their name, ID or permit number, birth details, address, sex and a face image. Signing up would be voluntary, and the bill sets data protection rules, bans on tracking and commercial or political use of ID data, fines for service providers that break the rules, and a complaints process. Some words in the scanned text are hard to read, so a few details are uncertain.
whyItMatters: A legal digital ID could become the usual way to log in to government and private services, and this bill decides who can see your identity data and what they may do with it. It also says you cannot be forced to use the digital ID, and that registration and getting an ID number are free.
keyProvisions: Articles 19 to 22: set up the Maldives Digital Identity System, linked to the existing ID card, Vaarutha portal and visa databases, and make Maldives Digital Services responsible for running it; Article 23 has the minister form a policy advisory committee within 90 days

Articles 27 and 31: Maldivian ID card holders, foreigners with work permits and their visa-holding dependants may register by giving name, ID or permit number, date and place of birth, sex, addresses and a face image (phone and email optional); Article 34 lets people leave the system at any time
Article 28: the system's database must be encrypted and run from data centres in the Maldives, with backups allowed abroad if they meet international standards
Article 43: nobody can be required to create or use a digital ID to get a service, and providers must offer another way to get the service, with exemptions for some small or online-only businesses

Articles 57 to 60: certain personal details may only be shared with the person's consent, ID data may not be used for marketing, profiling, tracking or political campaigns, and data may go to law enforcement only in set cases such as an ongoing prosecution or a court order

Articles 67 to 69: service providers and data processors that break the law can be fined up to MVR 500,000 for a first breach and MVR 500,000 to 1,000,000 for repeat breaches; registration and issuing ID numbers or authenticators must be free
whoIsAffected: Maldivians and foreign residents who use services that check identity, the government offices and businesses that would rely on the system, and Maldives Digital Services, which would run it.
statedReasons: The government says the bill sets up a secure, easy digital identity system for verifying identity in online dealings with state bodies, legal persons and others. It also sets rules to use technology fully while protecting the data used and keeping the system secure and trusted.
